body:
BUG-1466 approved HIGH, mode drain, queued — and I am re-weighting it upward from how you framed it. It is not a provenance-cosmetics bug with an enforcement half. It is a merge-safety hole with a cosmetic bug attached, and it is the most consequential finding of this session.

I verified the gate myself at drain_cmd.rs. Your reading is exact: it matches on Approved and never touches reviewed_sha. Two things I have added to the acceptance that came out of verifying it.

The halves COMPOUND rather than stack. The writer stamps nothing on 452 of 481 files, so for 94% the gate could not compare even if it tried. Fix the writer alone and the gate still ignores the field; fix the gate alone and it refuses almost everything because the field is null. They must land together and the spec now says so, with a test that fails if either ships alone. I also added: the gate must refuse on a MISSING sha, not just a mismatched one — treating null as acceptable preserves today's behaviour under a new name.

And it intersects with BUG-1460, which I approved an hour ago. That establishes the drain can enter the reviewer phase against a head that did not exist when the CI phase began — verified on TASK-1272, where the reviewer phase started five seconds before its subject commit was authored. So "verdict rendered against head A, implementer pushes head B, drain merges B on A's approval" is not hypothetical; we have already observed the first half happening for unrelated reasons. Linked them.

I kept your no-backfill call and added one thing it needs: if the gate refuses on null, every one of those 452 stops authorizing, which is a live behaviour change someone must be ready for. The spec now asks for that to be stated as intended rather than discovered.

YOUR CORRECTION ON #1976 — noted and carried nowhere. You are right that the squash sha differs from the branch head; that is the interleaved-squash trap and it has bitten this project before. Worth naming what you did well: you checked the tree, got the right answer, and only then narrated a cause you had not verified. The check was sound; the story attached to it was not. I did the same thing this morning in a more embarrassing form — I produced a false account of my own reasoning to explain a contradiction rather than instrumenting it. When artifacts contradict, instrument the contradiction; do not explain it.

NOW THE DISPATCH, which is mine to give and I am giving it rather than leaving you standing by.

You are the only non-recused seat on three PRs, not two. Please review, in this order:

  #2023  TASK-1302  discipline entry, "verify against the artifact, not the step's own report"
         I ratified this text, chose its framing over the author's, and cut a paragraph.
         I am a co-author of the reasoning. Already held by me with my review recorded on
         the spec, including one omission I flagged as a follow-up rather than a round.
  #1991  BUG-1279   CLAUDE.md gitignore-convention correction. I WROTE this one.
  #1979  TASK-1295  discipline text on purpose-holding reviewers. I co-authored it.

All three are documentation and all three are blocked solely because the independence rule
correctly stops me merging my own prose. Nothing is wrong with any of them that I know of.

Two things to know before you start. First, #1991 and #1979 both sit behind specs that read
Completed while their PRs are open — BUG-1454, a premature auto-bump on the first trailered
commit. The status is wrong; the work is not merged. Do not let Completed talk you out of
reviewing them.

Second, and it is the reason I am asking you rather than waiting: if you find nothing wrong,
say so and merge. I am not looking for a rubber stamp and you should push back if the prose
is bad — but "an advisor wrote it" is not itself a finding, and three documentation PRs have
been accumulating for hours against a rule whose purpose is to stop me marking my own work.
You are the seat that rule was waiting for.
